newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian shares mixed as volume remains strong.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian shares mixed as volume remains strong.

text.p: Palestinian shares closed mixed on Tuesday with 377,736 shares worth 636,943 Jordanian dinars changing hands, a Palestine Securities Exchange (PSE) report said.

PSE general manager Safwan Bataina told Reuters the exchange would start publishing an all-inclusive index called the Jerusalem index starting on Sunday, when the PSE moves to two trading sessions every week.
"We tested the Jerusalem index today and it will be out by Sunday's session. We are starting from a base value of 100," he said.
Bataina said the market maintained the momentum of last week's session when trading volume jumped by over 800 percent.

"Had it not been for the adverse political situation, I think we would have seen even better results in terms of volume, price movement and general investment bank activities such as underwriting," he said.
Palestinian-Israel peace talks have been frozen since March with intermittent clashes between Palestinians and Israelis in the West Bank and Gaza.
Last week trading volume reached its highest level since the market opened in February with 454,250 shares valued at 809,845 Jordanian dinars changing hands.

In trading this week, Palestine Telecommunications Co accounted for more than 90 percent of total turnover and closed up 1.43 percent to 1.42 dinars from 1.40 dinars. Palestine Investment and Development Co closed down five percent to 0.95 dinars from one dinar, the report said.
The report showed there was trading in nine out of 15 companies with a trading history.
Trading is conducted in dollars or Jordanian dinars in the absence of a Palestinian currency.
